message.text: The change gives each fallback a thinking level of its own, `{ model, thinking }`, and lets a preference file change it. The lineage it records when such a fallback answers still compares only the route-level `thinking`. `leaving` works out `thinking` from `planned.thinking` against `policy.thinking` (lines 650–659). The only per-model fact it adds is `answeredAt` (lines 665–672), which is the fallback entry's own level from the effective route. It never records the level committed policy gives that model, or which file changed it. If a preference removes a fallback's level, `answeredAt` is absent, so the lineage says nothing about any level change.

evidence.snippet:
A committed `thinking: high` must not become `off` through preferences when policy refuses model overrides.
The existing `acceptOverridden: false` guard also refuses a changed thinking level, before a model runs.
Moving a lens to another tier retains its committed tier's policy for models and thinking.
Where policy accepts overrides, check lineage records the effective level, committed level and source file.
Unset remains distinct from off. Thinking-only preferences still allow model derivation.

heavy:
    model: openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol
    thinking: low
    fallbacks: [{ model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5, thinking: medium }, { model: openai/gpt-5.5, thinking: low }]
    accept: [openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol, anthropic/claude-opus-5-5, openai/gpt-5.5]

explanation.what: The change gives each fallback a thinking level of its own, `{ model, thinking }`, and lets a preference file change it. The lineage it records when such a fallback answers still compares only the route-level `thinking`. `leaving` works out `thinking` from `planned.thinking` against `policy.thinking` (lines 650–659). The only per-model fact it adds is `answeredAt` (lines 665–672), which is the fallback entry's own level from the effective route. It never records the level committed policy gives that model, or which file changed it. If a preference removes a fallback's level, `answeredAt` is absent, so the lineage says nothing about any level change.
explanation.whatToDo: When the answering model's effective level (its own entry's level, else the route's) differs from the level committed policy gives that model (`ReviewPlan.ownLevel(policy, model)`, else the committed route's level), record it in lineage the way a route-level override is recorded. Include the effective level, the committed level and the file that set it, for example by filling `CheckLineage.thinking` with the per-model levels. Then make `describeLineage` and doctor print it. Alternatively, amend `thinking-override-policy` in a decision that says why that lineage is no longer owed.
explanation.whyHere: The active base decision `2026-10-19-thinking-override-policy.md` (line 8) says: "Where policy accepts overrides, check lineage records the effective level, committed level and source file." Under `acceptOverridden: false` this change treats a re-levelled fallback as a thinking override (rule 3 drops it). Under the default it accepts the same override but records neither the committed level nor its source. The head decision amends `tier-thinking-routes`, `reasoning-low…`, `lens-routes` and `design-lens-on-codex-route`, but not `thinking-override-policy`. So the base rule still governs, and the change keeps the guard half of it and drops the lineage half. The case that drops out is exactly the one this change exists for: a Claude fallback run at `low`.

properties.failureScenario: Committed `melian.yaml` has `heavy: { model: openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol, thinking: low, fallbacks: [{ model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5, thinking: medium }] }`, as this change sets Melian's own heavy tier, and `acceptOverridden` is left at its default. A maintainer's `melian.local.yaml` writes `heavy: { fallbacks: [anthropic/claude-opus-5-5] }`. Arrays replace on merge (config.ts `merge`), so the effective route is Sol at `low`, then a bare Opus, with `by = melian.local.yaml`. Sol reaches its usage limit and the lens fails over to Opus. Opus runs at `low`, the starving level the decision was written to prevent, where committed policy wanted `medium`. `judge` → `leaving(policy, opus, "melian.local.yaml", planned)` finds `level === wantedThinking` (`low === low`), so `thinking` is undefined. `answeredAt` is undefined because the bare entry names none. The stored lineage is `{ model: opus, wanted: sol, by: "melian.local.yaml", outside: false }`. `describeLineage` renders "on anthropic/claude-opus-5-5, set by melian.local.yaml, where policy wants openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol and accepts anthropic/claude-opus-5-5", with no mention that the level changed from `medium` to `low`. If the preference instead sets Opus `thinking: high`, the lineage says "it answered at thinking high" but still not that policy wanted `medium`. In both cases the verdict and doctor hide an accepted thinking override that the base decision says lineage must record.
